subject: general
question: A sum of ₹400 lent at compound interest amounts to ₹484 in 2 years, interest compounded yearly. What is the rate of interest p.a.?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **2-year** period, the ratio of **Principal (P)** to **Amount (A)** is used by taking the **square root**.

Ratio of P : A → 400 : 484

Divide by 4 → 100 : 121

Square root for 1 year → √100 : √121 = 10 : 11

Interest for 1 year = 11 − 10 = 1 unit

Rate % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹400

**Amount (A)** = ₹484

**Time (n)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/523e0e33cb96598d598fb045cd7474d9f1a1e8c12db2ce4b96dff8d15a693837.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 484 = 400(1 + R/100)²

⇒ 484 ÷ 400 = (1 + R/100)²

⇒ 121 ÷ 100 = (1 + R/100)²

⇒ √(121 ÷ 100) = 1 + R/100

⇒ 11 ÷ 10 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = (11 ÷ 10) − 1

⇒ R/100 = 1 ÷ 10

⇒ R = (1 × 100) ÷ 10

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The total amount A is given by A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt, where n is the number of times interest is compounded per year.

Effective Rate of Interest

When interest is compounded more than once a year, the effective rate is higher than the nominal rate: E = (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1.

CI vs SI for 2 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by: D = P(R/100)².

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate how long it takes to double your money: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Interest Rate.
